body:
The `execute` tool reports `Command succeeded` when a pipeline, a `;` chain, `||`, or `&` hides a failing command behind a status that is not its own.

## The problem

A shell reports the exit status of the last command it ran. When an agent filters output for brevity — `pytest ... 2>&1 | tail -15`, a linter piped to `head`, a check followed by `; echo done` — the last command is the filter, and the filter succeeds. The failing command's status is gone.

`execute` passes that zero through and labels it:

```
2 failed, 10 passed

[Command succeeded with exit code 0]
```

The output is still there to read. The problem is the label directly under it, which states the opposite, on exactly the commands that decide whether work is finished. An agent that trusts the status line concludes the tests passed.

comments.body:
Hi @mdrxy, I'd like to work on this.

My proposed fix is to make the execute trailer describe only what the shell can actually prove (for example, `Command completed with exit code 0`) instead of claiming the whole compound command succeeded. A shell only exposes the final/aggregate status after constructs such as pipelines, `;`, `||`, and `&`, so rewriting that status as “succeeded” is misleading. I would update the sync and streaming formatters together and add regression coverage for masked-failure compound commands.

If you prefer enforcing shell options such as `pipefail` instead, I'm happy to adjust. Could you assign this issue to me?

@liuxusummer this is yours, you asked first and I'm not going to cut across it. I'd reproduced this before I saw your comment and went a fair way down the wrong road, so posting what that cost me in case it's useful.

Short version: I think your instinct to describe rather than reinterpret is right, and I'd argue against the `pipefail` fallback you offered.

`pipefail` fixes the reported case and breaks a more common one, because a reader that exits early sends SIGPIPE to the writer:

| command | today | with `pipefail` |
|---|---|---|
| `sh -c 'echo out; exit 1' \| tail -1` | 0 | 1 (the bug, fixed) |
| `seq 1 100000 \| head -3` | 0 | 141 |
| `yes \| head -1` | 0 | 141 |
| `seq 1 100000 \| grep -q 5` | 0 | 141 |

I then tried what looks like the obvious refinement. Read `PIPESTATUS`, treat SIGPIPE on a non-final stage as benign, report the first stage that really failed. It passes all of the above, so I believed it for about a day. It's also wrong:

| command | today | that rule |
|---|---|---|
| `grep zzz /etc/hosts \| wc -l` | 0 | 1 |
| `diff a b \| head -2` | 0 | 1 |
| `git diff --quiet \| cat` | 0 | 129 |

The SIGPIPE carve-out only rescues stages killed by a closed pipe. It does nothing for the much larger family of tools that exit non-zero as information: grep with no match, diff finding differences, cmp, `git diff --quiet`. "Count the matches" and "show me the diff" are at least as common as `pytest | tail`, so it trades one false-failure class for another of about the same size.

Generalising, nothing at this layer can tell `pytest` exiting 1 from `grep` exiting 1. They're the same integer, and the thing that separates them is what the tool meant by it, which never gets transmitted. Any rule that rewrites the status has to guess, and the guess is wrong often enough to hurt. That's the argument for your version. Describing what the shell can prove can't invent a failure.

The one gap I'd flag in it is that `_execute_artifact` publishes `{"exit_code": response.exit_code}` as a structured artifact, so the agent still receives a literal `0` beside the text however the trailer is worded. If the goal is that the agent stops concluding the tests passed, the wording alone may not get there.

What seems to thread it, offered as an idea rather than a request, is to report the stages without judging them, since the agent can judge. It chose the command.

```
2 failed, 10 passed

[Command completed with exit code 0]
Pipeline stages exited: 1, 0
```

Exit code untouched, so no invented failures, and the information the shell dropped is now in front of the agent. I prototyped it and checked 11 shapes against plain `sh`: zero exit-code divergences, and `pytest ... | tail` carries `1, 0`. Worth saying that this only improves the odds rather than guaranteeing anything, since it depends on the model actually reading the line. If you want the patch to crib from, say the word and I'll push the branch. Equally happy for you to ignore it.

Two things that will bite if you do go near bash. `PIPESTATUS` needs it, and POSIX `sh` is `dash` on Debian, so it needs a fallback. And wrapping the command at all defeats bash's exec optimisation, so a timed-out command stops being killed. `sleep 25` with a 2s timeout returned 124 and left the process running. That one needs a process-group kill and isn't obvious until you look for it.

Last thing, unrelated to whichever fix lands: `BaseSandbox`'s capture wrapper records `$?` of a subshell, so a pipeline's status is masked there too.

Pushed the branch I mentioned, as a draft PR so it's easier to read than a patch: #5997. Still not asking for it to be merged, and #5955 is still @liuxusummer's.

Two things in it turned out to be worth more than the diff. The exit code is deliberately left alone, because rewriting it cannot be made correct. And wrapping the command to read `PIPESTATUS` stops bash `exec`-ing it in place, which quietly changes what the timeout has to kill: my first attempt at that returned on time but left the process running, and my second returned twenty seconds late on `echo hi; sleep 20 &`. Worth knowing before anyone goes near that code, whichever fix lands.

Hi @mdrxy, I would like to work on this issue if it is still available. The current `LocalShellBackend.execute` path passes `subprocess.run(..., shell=True).returncode` through to `ExecuteResponse` and the middleware trailer, so a command such as `sh -c 'exit 1' | tail -1` can emit failing output alongside a success claim. I would keep the raw aggregate `exit_code` unchanged rather than enabling `pipefail`, and would expose only status information the shell can prove (or otherwise make the warning explicit) across the sync/streaming execute paths without changing command semantics.

Planned validation is focused unit coverage for masked pipelines and compound commands, ordinary successful/non-zero commands, quoted operators and redirections, plus the async/streaming paths and the existing `deepagents` format/lint checks. I also reviewed the closed reference PRs #5943 and #5997 and will avoid their status-rewriting and timeout-regression approaches. If the existing informal claim by @liuxusummer is not being formalized, could you please assign the issue to me and confirm the preferred scope?

Hi @mdrxy, I would like to work on this issue if it is still available.

The current `FilesystemMiddleware` execute formatting path turns any `exit_code == 0` into `[Command succeeded with exit code 0]`, even when the shell status comes from a later stage or command. That can mislead an agent after commands such as `pytest ... 2>&1 | tail -15`, `false; echo done`, or a backgrounded command. I reviewed the closed reference PRs #5943 and #5997: changing shell semantics (`pipefail`/pipeline-status wrapping) risks false failures and timeout/process-group regressions, while #5997 also leaves the broader middleware formatting path unaddressed.

If assigned, I propose a focused fix in the shared execute-result formatter: preserve the raw `artifact.exit_code` and command behavior, but avoid an unqualified success claim when syntax indicates that the zero may be masked; keep ordinary zero/non-zero commands unchanged and cover sync, async, and capture-offload formatting. The regression tests would exercise pipelines, `;`/newline chains, `||`, backgrounding, quoted operators, redirects, comments, and the unchanged artifact/status behavior. I will keep this limited to one package and will not change `uv.lock` or add dependencies.

Could you please assign the issue to `UniversePeak` and confirm whether this status-description approach is the preferred scope? I will wait for formal assignment before creating a branch or implementation.
I can take this if the existing claimant is no longer pursuing it. Please assign it to @abhinavkr26104 if available; I will wait for assignment before coding.
